subject: Hosted→Dedicated: Crestline onramp — sizing validation & cutover windows
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Palmer <emma.palmer@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration — initial sizing ask and validation plan

Hi Emma,

Great meeting yesterday — thanks for walking through Crestline's SLA profile and the peak shapes. To make sure the Dedicated onramp goes smoothly, we need two quick inputs from your engineering team so we can lock the capacity request and schedule the staging cutover: 

1) A 7-day minute-level traffic sample (preferably counts of generation requests by model type; a single JSON export is fine).
2) Any blackout/maintenance windows between Nov 1–Nov 10 that would block a 4-hour migration window.

On our side we'll run a sizing validation with continuous-batch simulation and a light canary (10% of traffic) before cutting over. Attached is the capacity-matrix-v3.xlsx template we typically use; if you can populate the 95th/99th percentiles for token length and qps by Tue EOD (Oct 29) we'll have a validated capacity baseline by Oct 30.

Proposed tentative cutover slots (we can shift):
- Nov 3 02:00–06:00 UTC (preferred by infra teams)
- Nov 4 22:00–02:00 UTC (backup)

I'll coordinate runbook delivery and a final ops call.

Best,
Jonas
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: capacity-matrix-v3.xlsx

From: Emma Palmer <emma.palmer@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated migration — initial sizing ask and validation plan

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the clear checklist.

Quick answers:
- We attached a 7-day snapshot (traffic-snapshot-20261027.json) and a short summary: average qps 85, 95th 210, daily peak window 09:00–11:00 PT, median response token length 42, 95th token length 270.
- No planned blackouts Nov 1–10 at the moment; we do have a backup maintenance window Nov 6 if needed.

Procurement: we are reviewing your Dedicated contract template and will loop back on PO timing.

Can you confirm what fallback model you plan to expose during canary (hosted fallback vs reduced-quantized variant)? That matters for our functional testing.

—Emma
VP Engineering, Crestline Health
emma.palmer@crestlinehealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted→Dedicated migration — initial sizing ask and validation plan

Team — forwarding Emma's snapshot. Key numbers: 95th qps 210, 95th token 270, preferred cutover Nov 3 window but they can do Nov 6 if pushed.

Karthik — can you run a quick right-size run using these inputs and confirm:
- GPU pool target (A100 80GB equiv or H100?)
- Expected sustained token/s and per-GPU concurrency assumptions (we want a 99.9th latency SLO headroom)
- Canary plan: 10% traffic mirrored for staging, healthcheck endpoints, auto-fallback to hosted endpoint if latency > 800ms for 2 consecutive minutes.

Marissa — I told Emma we'll share the runbook and a canary checklist. I'm attaching a draft capacity sheet populated with our current conversions. Please update the performance knobs (kv-cache, batch timeouts) before we send to Crestline.

Jonas

--- Forwarded message attached for context ---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Palmer <emma.palmer@crestlinehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated migration — initial sizing ask and validation plan

Emma — thanks for the snapshot. I've attached the Crestline cutover runbook (crestline-cutover-runbook.pdf) and the SLA redline summary (crestline-sla-delta.docx). Highlights and asks: 

- Sizing: based on your 95th numbers, we recommend allocating 6 H100-equivalent GPUs with the following guardrails: 12 max concurrent sessions per GPU, 4 token-slice batch timeouts, and prefix-KV caching enabled for frequent intents. See capacity-matrix-v3.xlsx tab "proposed".
- Canary: 10% mirrored traffic for 4 hours in staging with synthetic traffic ramp from 0→10% over 30 minutes, healthchecks every 60s (latency, error rate, token drift). If latency breach > 800ms for 2m or error rate > 0.5% for 5m, automatic rollback to hosted variant.
- Cutover windows: proposing Nov 4 02:00–06:00 UTC to align with our infra staffing; we can hold a fallback Nov 6 window as you suggested.
- Ops call: scheduling a runbook walk-through Tue Nov 2 17:00 PT (join link in Drive doc).

Procurement: to guarantee capacity for Nov 4 we need a signed PO or commitment by Nov 2 EOD. If procurement needs more time, we can provision a temporary burst (best-effort) but with no SLA guarantees.

Attaching: crestline-cutover-runbook.pdf, crestline-sla-delta.docx, capacity-matrix-v3.xlsx

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Onboarding | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Procurement <procurement@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Palmer <emma.palmer@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 09:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated migration — initial sizing ask and validation plan

Marissa / Jonas — thanks for the materials. A couple of items before we can issue PO by Nov 2: 

1) We need a short SOC2 evidence packet and current uptime history for the last 90 days (this is standard for our procurement board).
2) On SLA redlines: the team flagged the rollback credit language; we would prefer a trial period with performance SLAs applied after 30 days of stable metrics rather than immediate financial credits. Please advise if Redwood can accommodate a 30-day burn-in.

If Redwood can provide the SOC2 packet and accept the 30-day burn-in, we will aim to get PO to you by EOD Nov 2. Otherwise we will need to request the Nov 6 fallback window.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Crestline Health
procurement@crestlinehealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Palmer <emma.palmer@crestlinehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated migration — initial sizing ask and validation plan

Emma / Procurement — quick update to confirm next steps and the Nov 4 cutover window: 

- SOC2 / uptime packet: Neha will attach the SOC2 evidence bundle and 90-day uptime summary to the Drive folder by EOD today.
- SLA: Redwood can accept a 30-day burn-in for SLA financial credits. During the burn-in, we will run full monitoring and provide daily digest reports; credits become active on day 31 contingent on meeting the agreed SLOs.
- Capacity: Karthik validated the sizing and confirmed 6 H100-equivalent GPUs staged in the us-west-2 pool; we've reserved the Nov 4 02:00–06:00 UTC slot pending PO. If PO is delayed beyond Nov 2, we'll fall back to Nov 6 and provide best-effort burst capacity until then.

Final ops things: I've included the Drive runbook link in the runbook PDF and added the on-call contacts in section 4. Please confirm PO timing and whether Nov 4 remains acceptable. Once we have PO, Marissa will issue the final runbook and a calendar invite for the Nov 4 01:30 UTC pre-cutover check.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Crestline live on Dedicated.

Jonas
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123
